Definition: from the same as G3993 (through the idea of pinching toil; "pine"); to famish (absolutely or comparatively); figuratively, to crave:--be an hungered.
BiblicalUsage: Peinao means to hunger, to famish. Jesus blesses those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled, and He says the hungry will be fed at the judgment — “I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat.” He calls Himself the bread of life, and promises that whoever comes to Him shall never hunger.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that hunger is the appetite God put in us so we would seek Him: physical hunger points to the bread, and spiritual hunger points to the Bread of Life. I hold that the man who hungers after righteousness will be filled, not disappointed — God does not stir an appetite He will not satisfy. And the test of my hunger is whether I feed the hungry: Christ counts their meal as His own.
